claim: The General Assembly meets in regular session every year, convening no later than the second Wednesday of January
quote: shall meet in regular session at 10 a.m. no later than the second Wednesday of January of each year

claim: Regular sessions are limited to 120 calendar days
quote: Regular sessions of the general assembly shall not exceed one hundred twenty calendar days

claim: A bill not returned within ten days of presentment becomes law without signature
quote: If any bill shall not be returned by the governor within ten days after it shall have been presented to him, the same shall be a law

claim: After the session adjourns, the governor has thirty days to file a veto, or the bill becomes law
quote: office of the secretary of state, within thirty days after such adjournment, or else become a law

claim: An act takes effect on the date it states, or on passage if none is stated
quote: An act of the general assembly shall take effect on the date stated in the act, or, if no date is stated in the act, then on its passage

claim: Referendum petitions against an act may be filed up to ninety days after the session ends
quote: secretary of state not more than ninety days after the final adjournment of the session of the general assembly that passed the bill

claim: The Election Code governs general, primary, school district and special district elections, and municipal elections held as part of a coordinated election except where a charter conflicts
quote: This code applies to any municipal election conducted as part of a coordinated election except to the extent that this code conflicts with a specific charter provision

claim: The general election is the Tuesday after the first Monday of November in even-numbered years
quote: means the election held on the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday of November in each even-numbered year

claim: The primary is held on the last Tuesday in June of even-numbered years
quote: a primary election shall be held on the last Tuesday in June of even-numbered years

claim: County commissioners are elected at the general election for four-year terms, staggered
quote: and all of such commissioners shall be elected for the term of four years

claim: County clerk, sheriff, coroner, treasurer, surveyor and assessor are elected for four-year terms at the same time as the legislature
quote: one county clerk, who shall be ex officio recorder of deeds and clerk of the board of county commissioners; one sheriff; one coroner; one treasurer who shall be collector of taxes; one county surveyor; one county assessor

claim: County officer terms are four years
quote: The term of office of all such officials shall be four years

claim: The county attorney is appointed by the board, not elected
quote: when the interests of the county require it, may employ an attorney

claim: Regular school board elections are held on the first Tuesday in November of odd-numbered years
quote: the regular biennial school election in each school district shall be held the first Tuesday in November of each odd-numbered year

claim: School boards have five, six or seven directors, elected at the odd-year election for four-year terms
quote: five, six, or seven school directors shall be elected, the number having been established as required by law

claim: Directors serve four-year terms, though districts that had six-year terms in 1999 may keep them
quote: each for a term of four years and until a successor has been elected and qualified

claim: All school directors are voted on by the whole district, even under a director district plan, except in Denver and a few listed cases
quote: all school directors shall be voted on at large by the eligible electors of the entire school district, regardless of the school district

claim: Denver Public Schools has a seven-member board: five from director districts and two at large
quote: a seven-member board of education with one eligible elector elected from each of five director districts and two eligible electors elected from the district at large

claim: Regular special district elections are held on the Tuesday after the first Monday of May in odd-numbered years
quote: regular special district elections must be held on the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday of May in every odd-numbered year

claim: Special district directors serve four-year terms on boards of five or seven
quote: the basic term of office for directors, after the original terms provided in subsection (2) of this section, is four years

claim: Special district boards have five or seven members
quote: In the case of a seven-member board

claim: Statutory towns hold regular elections on the first Tuesday of April in even years; statutory cities on the first Tuesday of November in odd years
quote: the election held in towns on the first Tuesday of April in each even-numbered year; the election held in cities on the first Tuesday of November in each odd-numbered year

claim: A municipality may keep a different regular election date its voters chose
quote: the date on which the regular election of officers takes place as determined by the registered electors of the municipality

claim: Voters may move a municipality's regular election to November of odd or even years
quote: the question of whether the regular election date of such municipality shall be changed to either the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday of November in each odd-numbered year

claim: Elections held the same November day by overlapping governments are coordinated and run by the county clerk and recorder by mail ballot
quote: the county clerk and recorder is the coordinated election official

claim: Running in a coordinated election alongside partisan races does not make a nonpartisan election partisan
quote: as a part of a coordinated election does not cause an otherwise nonpartisan election of another political subdivision to become a partisan election

claim: An uncontested nonpartisan election may be canceled and the candidates declared elected
quote: there are not more candidates than offices to be filled at the election, including candidates filing affidavits of intent, the designated election official, if instructed by resolution of the governing body, shall cancel the election and declare the candidates elected

claim: A special district election may likewise be canceled when uncontested
quote: the designated election official, if instructed by resolution of the governing body, shall cancel the election and declare the candidates elected

claim: A primary may be canceled when no party has more than one candidate for any office
quote: the designated election official may cancel the primary election and declare each candidate the party nominee for that office at the general election

claim: Only major parties nominate by primary
quote: only a major political party, as defined in section 1-1-104 (22), is entitled to nominate candidates in a primary election

claim: County officers of major parties are nominated by primary
quote: all elective state, district, and county officers, and members of the general assembly shall be made by primary elections

claim: Unaffiliated voters may vote in one major party primary without joining it
quote: is entitled to vote in the primary election of a major political party without affiliating with that political party

claim: Unaffiliated voters are mailed every major party ballot and may return only one; returning more than one voids them all
quote: If an elector casts and returns to the clerk the ballot of more than one major political party, all such ballots returned will be rejected and will not be counted

claim: A party may switch to nominating by assembly or convention if three-fourths of its state central committee votes to
quote: if at least three-fourths of the total membership of the party's state central committee votes to use the assembly or convention nomination process

claim: Primary nominees are chosen by plurality
quote: receive a plurality of the votes cast shall be the respective party nominees for the respective offices

claim: A partisan election is one in which candidates appear with their affiliation
quote: means an election in which the names of the candidates are printed on the ballot along with their affiliation

claim: Elected nonpartisan local officials are nominated by petition
quote: for all elected nonpartisan local government officials must be by petition for nomination as provided in part 8 of this article

claim: Nonpartisan ballots carry no party designation
quote: The names shall be printed on the ballot without political party designation

claim: School director candidates are nominated by petition under the nonpartisan petition rules
quote: together with a nomination petition according to the provisions of section 1-4-803

claim: Special district candidates self-nominate
quote: shall file a self-nomination and acceptance form or letter signed by the candidate

claim: Statutory city and town candidates are nominated by petition without regard to party
quote: Candidates for municipal offices shall be nominated, without regard to affiliation, by petition on forms supplied by the clerk

claim: Statutory municipal ballots carry no party designation
quote: printed upon the ballot without political party designation

claim: A home rule charter controls all matters of municipal elections, including making them nonpartisan
quote: tending to make such elections or electoral votes non-partisan in character

claim: Nonpartisan ties for the most votes are settled by lot
quote: If any two or more candidates tie for the highest number of votes for the same office

claim: Statutory municipal winners are those with the greatest number of votes
quote: determine which persons have been by the greatest number of votes duly elected

claim: Local governments may use instant runoff voting for single-seat races
quote: the ranked voting method shall be known as instant runoff voting

claim: Statutory cities and towns and home rule municipalities may refer an instant runoff election into the coordinated election
quote: a statutory city or town or home rule municipality may refer a municipal election using instant runoff voting to be conducted as part of a coordinated election

claim: Candidates for partisan office who do not want a major party label are nominated by petition
quote: Candidates for partisan public offices to be filled at a general election who do not wish to affiliate with a major political party

claim: A petition-nominated unaffiliated candidate must have been unaffiliated or minor-party by the first business day of January of the election year
quote: registered as affiliated with a minor political party or as unaffiliated, as shown in the statewide voter registration system, no later than the first business day of the January immediately preceding the general election

claim: An unaffiliated candidate may not use a party name to identify themselves
quote: No name of any political party shall be used, in whole or in part, to identify an unaffiliated candidate

claim: County office petitions must be signed by voters of that county
quote: must be signed by eligible electors residing within the district or political subdivision in which the officer is to be elected

claim: Any eligible voter may sign an unaffiliated candidate petition, but not petitions for two candidates for the same office
quote: may be signed by any eligible elector who has not signed any other petition for any other candidate for the same office

claim: A municipal voter may not sign more than one nomination petition per office
quote: No registered elector shall sign more than one nomination petition for each separate office to be filled

claim: Counties under 70,000 people elect three commissioners; larger counties may have five
quote: when the population of any county shall equal or exceed seventy thousand, the board of county commissioners may consist of five members

claim: Each county is divided into three commissioner districts; each commissioner is elected from a district by the voters of the whole county
quote: One county commissioner must be elected from each of such districts by the voters of the whole county

claim: A county of 70,000 or more may go to five commissioners by referred or initiated vote
quote: the membership of the board of county commissioners may be increased from three to five members pursuant to this section

claim: Five-member counties may elect some commissioners only by district voters
quote: elected by the voters of the whole county or elected only by voters resident in the district from which the member runs for election

claim: County includes a city and county for Election Code purposes
quote: includes a city and county

claim: Voters of any county may adopt a home rule charter setting its organization and structure
quote: the registered electors of each county of the state are hereby vested with the power to adopt a home rule charter establishing the organization and structure of county government

claim: The constitutional rules on commissioners and county officers apply to a home rule county only as its charter provides
quote: shall apply to counties adopting a home rule charter only to such extent as may be provided in said charter

claim: A home rule county charter decides which officers are elected or appointed and their terms
quote: Officers of a home rule county shall be appointed or elected as provided for in the charter

claim: A home rule county must still provide all mandatory county functions
quote: A home rule county shall provide all mandatory county functions, services, and facilities

claim: The legislature classifies cities and towns, with no more than four classes
quote: The number of such classes shall not exceed four

claim: Municipalities are pre-1877 charter places, home rule places, and statutory cities and towns
quote: Cities or towns organized pursuant to the provisions of article XX of the state constitution

claim: A statutory city has over 2,000 people, or was a city in 1980 and stayed one, regardless of population
quote: means a municipal corporation having a population of more than two thousand

claim: A statutory town has 2,000 or fewer, or was a town in 1980 and stayed one, regardless of population
quote: means a municipal corporation having a population of two thousand or less

claim: A municipality organized as a town or city in 1980 keeps that organization regardless of population unless it reorganizes
quote: organized as a town on December 31, 1980, and choosing not to reorganize as a city

claim: A town entitled to become a city reorganizes only by electing city officers at a later regular election
quote: to organize according to the new classification available to it by the election of officers properly belonging thereto

claim: A statutory town is governed by a board of trustees of a mayor and six trustees
quote: consisting of one mayor and six trustees

claim: Town mayor and trustees serve two-year terms by default
quote: there shall be elected a mayor for a term of two years and six trustees for terms of two years

claim: A town board may adopt four-year overlapping terms by ordinance
quote: The board of trustees may provide by ordinance for four-year overlapping terms of office

claim: A town may reduce its trustees from six to four by vote
quote: may be reduced in number from six to four or again increased from four to six

claim: A statutory city elects a mayor, clerk and treasurer at large and two council members per ward, for two-year terms
quote: shall elect, at the regular election, a mayor, a clerk, and a city treasurer from the city at large

claim: Each ward of a statutory city elects two council members
quote: the registered electors of each ward of the city shall elect two members of the city council

claim: A city council may adopt four-year overlapping terms by ordinance
quote: The city council may provide by ordinance for four-year overlapping terms of office for council members

claim: Voters may make the city clerk and treasurer appointive
quote: that the position of city clerk or city treasurer, or both such positions, be made appointive rather than elective

claim: A statutory city may reorganize into council-manager form
quote: may reorganize into a city council-city manager form of municipal government

claim: A city or town of 2,000 or more may adopt a home rule charter
quote: having a population of two thousand inhabitants as determined by the last preceding census

claim: A home rule charter supersedes conflicting state law on local and municipal matters
quote: shall supersede within the territorial limits and other jurisdiction of said city or town any law of the state in conflict therewith

claim: Home rule charters control the creation and terms of municipal officers
quote: The creation and terms of municipal officers, agencies and employments

claim: Home rule charters control the date of municipal elections and nominations
quote: All matters pertaining to municipal elections in such city or town

claim: Any municipality may opt into the Election Code instead of the Municipal Election Code
quote: Any municipality may provide by ordinance or resolution that it will utilize the requirements and procedures of this code in lieu of

claim: Denver is a consolidated city and county
quote: are hereby consolidated and are hereby declared to be a single body politic and corporate, by the name of the

claim: Denver's charter sets which officers are elected and their terms
quote: The officers of the city and county of Denver shall be such as by appointment or election may be provided for by the charter

claim: Denver Public Schools elections are run by the Denver election commission
quote: shall be conducted and supervised by the election commission of the city and county

claim: Broomfield became a city and county in 2001, detached from Adams, Boulder, Jefferson and Weld counties
quote: shall be detached from the counties of Adams, Boulder, Jefferson, and Weld and shall be consolidated into a single county and municipal corporation

claim: Broomfield's officers are set by its charter and ordinances
quote: The officers of the city and county of Broomfield shall be as provided for by its charter or ordinances

claim: Special districts include fire protection, metropolitan and water districts
quote: means a special district which provides protection against fire by any available means

claim: A metropolitan district provides two or more services
quote: means a special district that provides for the inhabitants thereof any two or more of the following services

claim: A party member votes only their own party's primary ballot
quote: present the elector with the party ballot of the political party affiliation last recorded

claim: State statutes keep applying to home rule places except where the charter or its ordinances supersede them
quote: shall continue to apply to such cities and towns, except insofar as superseded by the charters of such cities and towns

claim: Home rule charters control nomination and election systems
quote: nomination and election systems

claim: Statutory municipalities are divided into cities and towns
quote: which have not chosen to adopt a home rule charter under the provisions of article XX of the state constitution, are divided into cities and towns
